findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/material-code-policy.ts:491 preflightMaterialCodeExclusions (the claimed second enforcement layer for excludePaths) is never called by resolveMaterialCodePolicy (lines 305-384) or by any handler/gate — grep across packages/main/src confirms its ONLY caller is the smoke test (packages/main/src/tasks/language-neutral-gates-smoke.ts:301,305), and there it is invoked directly with a hand-fabricated trackedFiles array, not derived from a real git tree at the resolved projectRoot. In real usage, resolveMaterialCodePolicy(dirRoot) for materialCode.excludePaths=["backend/"] does NOT throw (confirmed live: baseName("backend/")=="" so isImmutableManifestName never matches) — the smoke test itself even comments "backend/ passes basename resolve" before manually calling the isolated preflight function. So a project can save an excludePaths entry that covers a real manifest (e.g. backend/ over backend/go.mod) with NO error/warning at config-resolve time, contradicting: (1) the module docstring lines 13-17 ("enforced both at config-resolve time and by a filesystem-aware transition preflight"), (2) config.ts:58-59 MaterialCodeConfig docstring ("via the filesystem-aware preflight, covering"), and (3) checklist.json CHK-002 adversarial verificationEvidence ("rejected at BOTH layers"). Net classification correctness is still preserved for backend/go.mod itself because classifyMaterialCodePath checks the immutable-manifest step (step 1) before excludePaths (step 3) regardless of this preflight, but the promised REJECTION/error-surfacing behavior for misleading directory-level excludes never fires in production — the two-layer enforcement architecture the story claims is DONE is actually one layer.

doc-promise-undelivered: ProofStoryDiagnosticInput.materialClassification (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:144, consumed at proofstory.ts:710 via materialClassificationHasMaterialCode) is NEVER populated by any real production caller. Grep for materialClassification across packages/main/src shows it only appears in proofstory.ts (def+use), review-assurance-floor.ts (a DIFFERENT field on EvaluateReviewAssuranceFloorArgs), and the smoke test. All 5 real diagnosticInput/proofStoryDiagnosticInput builders that feed evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics in production — packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:129, packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts:110 (used by proofStoryDevGateFailure, the actual DEV-gate enforce path), packages/main/src/handlers/proofstory.ts:92, and packages/main/src/handlers/story-review.ts:229 and :733 — construct the ProofStoryDiagnosticInput object WITHOUT a materialClassification field and never call buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot. So in production, materialClassificationHasMaterialCode(input.materialClassification) always receives undefined and always returns false; the new `materialCodePresent` behavior-change signal at proofstory.ts:710 can never fire for real ProofStory evaluations. Only packages/main/src/tasks/language-neutral-gates-smoke.ts:146-170 (helper proofStoryInput()) and :210-211 manually construct an input WITH a hand-built snapshot to exercise this branch — that is not equivalent to production wiring. This directly contradicts checklist.json CHK-001 (marked done): the context text ("ProofStoryDiagnosticInput gains a materialClassification field consumed by the trigger predicate"), the userSees claim ("An identical bug story flips required=true across floor + repro + ProofStory triggers, all driven by one classification snapshot"), and the CHK-001:happy verificationEvidence note pointing at the RED harness (tmp/w1-red/red-language-degradation.cjs), which — confirmed by reading it — only calls classifyReviewAssuranceFloorPath and never exercises the repro-first or ProofStory trigger flag at all. A pure-.go/.py/.rs bug story therefore still does NOT flip ProofStory's red-evidence trigger in real usage; only the review-assurance floor classifier (and, independently, the repro-first gate via its own freshly-built snapshot in evaluateStoryEvidenceBindingGate) are genuinely wired end-to-end.

NEW regression (fix-round side effect): readMaterialCodeConfig (packages/main/src/core/material-code-policy.ts:348-364) throws MaterialCodePolicyError on ANY unparseable lattice.config.json (not just a malformed materialCode block), and this propagates UNCAUGHT through classifyReviewAssuranceFloorPath (review-assurance-floor.ts:490-496, calls resolveMaterialCodePolicy with no try/catch) and evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor (review-assurance-floor.ts:774: `listed.files.map(path => classifyReviewAssuranceFloorPath(...))`, no try/catch). Before this diff review-assurance-floor.ts never read lattice.config.json at all (confirmed: `git show main:packages/main/src/core/review-assurance-floor.ts` has zero loadConfig/config reads), so a malformed config file was harmless to the floor. Now 5 of the 6 real production callers of evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor have NO enclosing try/catch: machine.ts canFinishGuard (~line 769-831, the TEST->DONE transition guard) and getGuardFailureReason (~line 1002-1262); done-oracle.ts buildDoneChecklist (~line 861); handlers/review-escalation.ts review_escalation_status (~line 287); handlers/done-prepare.ts buildDonePrepareReviewAssurancePlan (~line 1254). Only handlers/transition-effects.ts renderReviewAssuranceBeforeDoneAdvisory (line 169-201) is protected by its own advisory try/catch. LIVE VERIFIED: built dist on this worktree AND a clean main checkout; created a fixture repo whose ONLY lattice.config.json defect is a plain JSON syntax error (trailing comma, no materialCode key at all, not even referencing this feature). On main, classifyReviewAssuranceFloorPath("x.ts", root) returns normally ({materialCode:true,...}). On this branch, evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor({projectRoot,gitCwd,changedFiles:["x.ts"],storyId,store}) throws uncaught: `MaterialCodePolicyError: material-code policy config invalid [lattice.config.json]: config file is not valid JSON...`. Net effect: for ANY project (TS-only or not, materialCode-configured or not) whose lattice.config.json has a JSON syntax error that loadConfig elsewhere in the codebase silently tolerates (per this storys own docstring at material-code-policy.ts:344, loadConfig swallows parse errors), lattice story_advance into DONE and other DONE-readiness commands (done_prepare, review_escalation_status, done-checklist rendering) now hard-fail with an opaque, feature-unrelated material-code-policy error instead of proceeding as before -- a new fail-closed blast radius far wider than this storys own CHK-002 adversarial scope (a malformed materialCode BLOCK fails closed) and inconsistent with the fix rounds own byte-identical-for-existing-projects framing (F-002 fix).

Maintainability/perf: packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts:414-425 runScopeTransitionGate calls result = runScopeGate(storyId, ctx.store, ctx.root, undefined, gitCwd) (line 416), which internally calls buildScopeDiffPack (scope-contract.ts:477, runScopeGate) whenever a scope contract already exists for the story, and then UNCONDITIONALLY calls buildScopeDiffPack(ctx.root, undefined, gitCwd) again (line 423) purely to build the semantic_analysis_unavailable degradation event via emitSemanticDegradationEvent (line 424). For any story with an existing scope contract (the common in-flight case), this recomputes the full main...HEAD unified diff plus TypeScript AST anchor parsing for every hunk TWICE per transition attempt instead of reusing the diffPack runScopeGate already built (runScopeGate does not currently return/expose its diffPack to the caller). Not a correctness bug -- both computations observe the same git state within one call -- but a real, avoidable doubling of an expensive git+AST computation on every DEV->REVIEW/REVIEW->TEST/TEST->DONE-adjacent scope transition for stories with a scope contract, introduced by this diff (this duplication pattern did not exist on main).

NEW regression (R2 fix-round side effect, unfixed second consumer of the same root cause): the R2 fix converted MaterialCodePolicyError into a structured ok:false outcome ONLY inside evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor (review-assurance-floor.ts:767-798), but readMaterialCodeConfig fail-closed-on-non-ENOENT (material-code-policy.ts:373-388) is shared low-level infrastructure ALSO reached, unprotected, by the repro-first evidence-binding gate: evaluateStoryEvidenceBindingGate (repro-evidence-binding-gate.ts:378, `buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot(projectRoot)` with no try/catch) and classifyReproFirstRequirement (repro-evidence-binding-gate.ts:116, `ensureFreshMaterialClassificationSnapshot`->`materialClassificationSnapshotStale` which ALSO throws per FIX 2). Confirmed LIVE against this worktrees rebuilt dist: a fixture git repo whose only lattice.config.json defect is a JSON syntax error (trailing comma, no materialCode key) makes `getGuardFailureReason(storyId, store, "PLAN", root)` and `getGuardFailureReason(storyId, store, "DEV", root)` (dist/core/machine.js, src at packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:1002, the repro-gate calls at lines 1054 and 1102) throw MaterialCodePolicyError UNCAUGHT -- the exact same function (`machine.ts getGuardFailureReason`) the R2 commit message explicitly names as now safe ("5 no-try/catch DONE-readiness callers (machine.ts canFinishGuard/getGuardFailureReason...) receive a named gate failure instead of an uncaught crash"). The fix only protects the LATER review-assurance-floor section of that function (used for the DONE target phase); the EARLIER repro-first-gate section (used for PLAN/DEV target phases, machine.ts:1054/1102) is untouched. Production call graph: transition-orchestrator.ts:585 `throw resolveGuardFailure(actor, args.storyId, store, args.phase, ctx.root)` -> phase-gates.ts:186 resolveGuardFailure -> phase-gates.ts:192 unwrapped `getGuardFailureReason(...)` call -- so any `lattice story_advance --phase=PLAN` or `--phase=DEV` on a story whose lattice.config.json has ANY non-ENOENT read/parse error (or now also an excludePaths/materialCode violation, since resolveMaterialCodePolicy itself throws for those, material-code-policy.ts:424-452) throws out of resolveGuardFailure as a raw MaterialCodePolicyError instead of the intended clean "Cannot enter PLAN/DEV: ..." guard message -- it is only caught by the CLIs generic top-level catch-all (cli-engine.ts ~1484), losing the [reason_code] tagging convention every other guard failure uses. Also unprotected: story-create.ts:125/1018/1076 (renderReproFirstStoryCreatePreflight -> buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot, no try/catch) used during story_create. Repro (built dist, same one CLI loads): node -e with buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot(root) and getGuardFailureReason(id,fakeStore,"PLAN",root) both throw for a repo whose only defect is a trailing-comma JSON error in lattice.config.json. This directly fails the rounds own adversarial ask ("verify BOTH: no silent defaults AND no uncaught throw") for the repro-first-gate half of the same root-cause fix.

packages/main/src/core/material-code-policy.ts:960-994 (buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot) + :436-449 (resolveMaterialCodePolicy split): the R4 FIX-1 config/tree split introduces a NEW fail-open regression for buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot — the tree-bound exclusion preflight (assertMaterialCodeExclusionsAgainstTree) is now only invoked `if (headRef)` inside the retry loop (line ~987); when currentGitHead(gitCwd) returns undefined (non-git projectRoot, pre-first-commit repo, or any wrapper-root/gitCwd resolution failure), the preflight is SKIPPED ENTIRELY and the snapshot is returned silently with the un-validated policy, instead of failing closed. This regresses from R3 behavior, where buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot called the OLD resolveMaterialCodePolicy(projectRoot) which ran preflightMaterialCodeExclusions synchronously and unconditionally (ref defaulted to HEAD, independent of later currentGitHead success) before the retry loop even started, so a non-git/unresolvable root with a covered exclusion always threw fail-closed. Empirically reproduced against the built HEAD dist: resolveMaterialCodePolicy(nonGitDirWithExcludePaths=[backend/]+realBackend/go.mod) still throws MaterialCodePolicyError as expected, but buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot(sameDir) returns a snapshot with NO throw and policy.excludePaths still containing [backend/] unvalidated. This directly affects the three production consumers of buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot that this story exists to protect: repro-evidence-binding-gate.ts:418 (evaluateStoryEvidenceBindingGate — the exact repro-first PLAN/DEV gate CHK-001 adversarial intent targets: "cannot regress to the config-blind call... fails closed"), story-create.ts:133 (STORY_INTAKE repro-first classification), and review-assurance-floor.ts:774 (the floor own snapshot-build path). None of the 29 language-neutral-gates-smoke checks (including R4-a/R4-b) exercise buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot on a root where currentGitHead fails with a policy excludePaths entry covering a real level-1 manifest, so this gap is untested. This violates the story background/plan invariant that the level-1 immutable manifest set is protected by TWO enforcement layers (config-resolve rejection + filesystem-aware transition preflight) for every consumer — the second layer is now conditionally bypassable for the snapshot-based consumers.

Test-coverage gap tied to lattice-review-quality F-006 (open, RR-015, verified, same round): CHK-001:adversarial:0 (repro classification fails closed on config-blind/regressed input) and CHK-002:adversarial:0 (excludePaths covering a real manifest is rejected at BOTH layers) verificationEvidence overstates what the automated smoke suite actually proves. language-neutral-gates-smoke.ts:376-383 tests fail-closed behavior for resolveMaterialCodePolicy(nonGitRoot) only; NO check in the 29-check suite (including R4-a/R4-b) calls buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot on a non-git-HEAD root with excludePaths covering a real level-1 manifest -- the actual production-consumed builder used by repro-evidence-binding-gate.ts, story-create.ts, and review-assurance-floor.ts. Live-reproduced against this worktree dist: resolveMaterialCodePolicy(nonGitDir) throws MaterialCodePolicyError as the smoke asserts, but buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot(sameNonGitDir) returns a snapshot with NO throw and policy.excludePaths still ["backend/"] unvalidated (material-code-policy.ts:978 `if (headRef)` guards the tree-bound preflight call, so an undefined headRef skips it entirely instead of failing closed). The must-priority adversarial verificationEvidence for CHK-001 and CHK-002 therefore does not concretely cover this reproducible fail-open path; add a smoke check for buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot+non-git-HEAD+covered-exclusion once F-006 is fixed.

packages/main/src/core/repro-evidence-binding-gate.ts:418 (evaluateStoryEvidenceBindingGate) + packages/main/src/handlers/story-create.ts:133 (STORY_INTAKE repro-first preflight) call buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot(projectRoot) with NO gitCwd override, so gitCwd internally defaults to projectRoot instead of the resolveGitCwd-resolved git ROOT that review-assurance-floor.ts consumers correctly thread (machine.ts:822/1262 via resolveGitCwd, done-oracle.ts:861, done-prepare.ts:1254, transition-effects.ts:180, review-escalation.ts:287). On a wrapper-root layout this defeats the R6 wrapper-root namespace fix for these two consumers: buildMaterialClassificationSnapshotAtRef computes namespacePrefix = projectRepoPrefix(gitCwd=projectRoot, projectRoot) = '' (identity, since gitCwd===projectRoot), but the git diff --name-status command it actually runs still emits TRUE repo-root-relative paths (e.g. project/bin/tool) regardless of which subdirectory cwd it is invoked from -- so the un-stripped git-namespace path leaks through as the snapshot file.path, and pathPrefixes/codeExtensions matching against it silently misclassifies material code as non-material. REPRODUCED against compiled dist: wrapper-root repo with gitRoot/project/bin/tool (extensionless executable script) changed in a main...feature diff; buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot(projectRoot) (exact call pattern of both call sites) yields path='project/bin/tool', materialCode=false, reason='default non-material'; correctly threading gitCwd = the real git root on the SAME diff yields path='bin/tool', materialCode=true, reason='extensionless shebang/executable script'. This means the repro-first DEV gate (wired via machine.ts:552,584,600,1054,1102 and handlers/session.ts:78) and the STORY_INTAKE repro-first preflight silently fail open on wrapper-root projects for exactly the class of material-code changes this story exists to classify correctly -- contradicting the module doc header's contract that review-assurance floor, repro-evidence-binding gate, and the ProofStory trigger all share one wrapper-root-safe classification snapshot boundary (only the floor consumer is actually wired through resolveGitCwd).
